speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly what happens during these episodes of unresponsiveness, and do you have any memory of them afterward?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does he experience any muscle stiffness, jerking movements, or loss of bladder control during these episodes? I also need to know if these events typically occur while he is awake, falling asleep, or waking up.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do the episodes typically occur during sleep or upon waking, and have you noticed any rhythmic jerking of his arms or legs? I would like to order an EEG to evaluate for seizure activity. REQUEST TEST: EEG

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history. No prior seizures or neurological evaluations. Social history: Enrolled in second grade. Lives with parents and one sibling. No reported use of medications or exposure to toxins.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, headache, visual or auditory disturbances, weakness, or other systemic symptoms. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Multiple sclerosis is highly unlikely in a 7-year-old with this specific presentation of focal seizures with aura. The "muddy taste" suggests a temporal lobe origin, so I need to confirm if there is any family history of epilepsy or recent head trauma. REQUEST TEST: Brain_MRI

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No evidence of mass lesions, infarctions, or structural abnormalities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI rules out structural causes like tumors or MS, so this is likely primary epilepsy, specifically temporal lobe epilepsy. I need to see the EEG results to confirm seizure activity and localize the focus. REQUEST TEST: EEG

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the temporal lobes, more prominent on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The EEG confirms right temporal lobe epilepsy, which aligns with the olfactory aura and clinical presentation. DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
